questions.question: What is a vertebrate? Name the five classes of vertebrates and the four features used to tell them apart.
questions.expected_answer: A vertebrate is an animal with a backbone (vertebral column) and an internal skeleton. The five classes are fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals. They are distinguished by body covering, how they breathe, how they control body temperature (ectothermic or endothermic) and how they reproduce.

questions.question: Compare amphibians and reptiles under the headings skin, breathing and eggs, and explain why reptiles can live in deserts.
questions.expected_answer: Skin: amphibians have smooth, moist skin with no scales; reptiles have dry skin with hard scales. Breathing: amphibian tadpoles breathe with gills and adults with lungs and moist skin; reptiles breathe with lungs all their lives. Eggs: amphibians lay soft, jelly-covered eggs in water, usually with external fertilisation; reptiles have internal fertilisation and lay shelled, leathery eggs on land. Reptiles can live in deserts because their scaly skin is waterproof and their shelled eggs do not dry out, so they do not need water to breed.

questions.question: Classify a dolphin, a bat and an ostrich, giving two reasons for each, and explain the difference between endothermic and ectothermic animals.
questions.expected_answer: Dolphin: mammal, because it breathes air with lungs, has hair at birth and feeds its young on milk. Bat: mammal, because it has fur and feeds its young on milk (it has no feathers). Ostrich: bird, because it has feathers and a beak and lays hard-shelled eggs, even though it cannot fly. Endothermic animals (birds and mammals) keep a constant body temperature using heat from respiration and need much food; ectothermic animals (fish, amphibians, reptiles) have a body temperature that changes with their surroundings.
